rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra on inna, the omitted conditional answer can be understood differently depending on whom the address of ترى targets: its hearer or the Prophet; one estimate is that the scene would be appalling.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالكسر، قدر الجواب: لقلت إن القوة على اختلاف القولين في المخاطب

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya estimates that seeing the wrongdoers at the moment they see and fear the punishment would make them admit all power belongs to God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: تقدير ذلك: ولو ترى الذين ظلموا، في حال رؤيتهم العذاب وفزعهم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He objects to Ibn Atiyya's wording and logic: the phrase should mean the time of their seeing, and the hearer's seeing them then does not entail their confession of God's power.
rows.anchor: وصار نظير قولك: يا زيد لو ترى عمرا في وقت ضربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the ya-reading with fatḥa, the answer may be that the wrongdoers would know God's power, or that the hearer would know it if the subject is implicit.
rows.anchor: وعلى من قرأ: ولو يرى، بالياء من أسفل وفتح، أن يكون تقدير الجواب: لعلموا

rows.speaker: الأخفش والمبرد
rows.claim: They place the omitted answer after the statement that God is severe in punishment; its wording varies with whether the subject is the hearer or the wrongdoers and with the reading.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي الحسن الأخفش، وأبي العباس المبرد، وتقديره: على قراءة ولو ترى بالخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the answer is placed at the verse's end, open أن is an object of يرى in the ya-reading and a causal complement in the address reading; kasra can still convey causation parenthetically.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن تكون معمولة ليرى في قراءة من قرأ بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With ya and both hamzas in kasra, إن may depend on an implicit saying as the answer, or begin a new statement while the answer remains omitted and ترى has an omitted object.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن تكون معمولة لقول محذوف هو جواب لو

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali allows ترى in the address reading to mean visual perception; the author also allows it to mean cognition.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي علي، ويحتمل أن تكون عرفانية

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: If أن is governed by يرى, it can mean 'know' and take two objects, with أن and its clause filling their place, according to Sibawayh.
rows.anchor: على مذهب سيبويه. والذين ظلموا، إشارة إلى متخذي الأنداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers may mean idol-makers specifically or unbelievers generally; the following context favors the idol-makers.
rows.anchor: لكن سياق ما بعده يرشد إلى أنهم متخذو الأنداد

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads إذ يرون in the passive, from the causative of رأى meaning to see.
rows.anchor: وقراءة ابن عامر: إذ يرون، مبنيا للمفعول، هو من أريت المنقولة من رأيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past إذ is inserted among future events to bring the event near and affirm its occurrence; Arabic poetry likewise uses past verbs under a future condition.
rows.anchor: ودخلت إذ، وهي للظرف الماضي، في أثناء هذه المستقبلات، تقريبا للأمر وتصحيحا لوقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted answer after لو is common in Qur'anic Arabic and ordinary Arabic, illustrated by three Qur'anic examples and a line of Imruʾ al-Qays.
rows.anchor: وحذف جواب لو، لفهم المعنى، كثير في القرآن، وفي لسان العرب

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ataa places the scene on Judgment Day: Hell approaches from five hundred years away and gathers the wrongdoers like a pigeon picking up grain, whereupon they know all power is God's.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: المعنى: ولو يرى الذين ظلموا يوم القيامة، إذ يرون العذاب حين تخرج إليهم جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says that knowing in this life what they will know on seeing punishment would make them renounce their rivals; the second seeing is direct visual sight.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لو يعلمون في الدنيا ما يعلمونه، إذ يرون العذاب، لأقروا بأن القوة لله جميعا

rows.speaker: التبريزي
rows.claim: Al-Tabrizi says that if they believed God can punish them on the Resurrection Day, they would avoid what incurs that punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال التبريزي: لو اعتقدوا أن الله يقدر ويقوى على تعذيبهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that recognizing God's exclusive power over reward and punishment, and seeing the torment, would produce indescribable remorse and knowledge of their error.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ولو يعلم هؤلاء الذين ارتكبوا الظلم العظيم بشركهم، أن القدرة كلها لله

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib reports that some took القوة as an appositive to الذين, yielding the sense of seeing God's power over the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: وحكى الراغب: أن بعضهم زعم أن القوة بدل من الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author judges the proposed apposition of القوة to الذين weak.
rows.anchor: قال: وهو ضعيف. انتهى. ويصير المعنى: ولو ترى قوة الله وقدرته

rows.speaker: المنتخب
rows.claim: Al-Muntakhab prefers the ya-reading because the Prophet and Muslims already know what unbelievers will witness, while the threatened unbelievers do not.
rows.anchor: وقال في المنتخب: قراءة الياء عند بعضهم أولى من قراءة التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sees no preference between the two readings because both the address and third-person forms are mass-transmitted.
rows.anchor: ولا فرق عندنا بين القراءتين، أعني التاء والياء، لأنهما متواترتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جميعا is a circumstantial accusative referring to the implicit pronoun in the governing prepositional phrase; القوة is a generic verbal noun meaning all powers belong to God.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب جميعا على الحال من الضمير المستكن في العامل في الجار والمجرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects taking جميعا as a circumstantial modifier of القوة because أن is the governor of القوة and does not govern that construction.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تكون حالا من القوة، لأن العامل في القوة أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When لو carries a wish-like sense and is followed by a فاء-answer, the expected subjunctive after an implicit أن is not attested without the فاء; لو is only secondarily wish-like by analogy with ليت.
rows.anchor: والسبب في ذلك أن كونها مشربة معنى التمني، ليس أصلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jussive after ليت without فاء is explained either by its implying a conditional sense or an omitted condition; لو is a derivative of a derivative, making that construction weaker.
rows.anchor: فصارت لو فرع فرع، فضعف ذلك فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In كما تبرأنا, the kāf is accusative as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun or as a circumstantial modifier of its implicit pronoun, and ما is a verbal noun clause: their disavowal matches ours.
rows.anchor: والكاف في كما: في موضع نصب، إما نعتا لمصدر محذوف

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows كما to modify an implied circumstantial state, paraphrased as 'disavowing in the same way.'
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: الكاف من قوله: كما في موضع نصب على النعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Ibn Atiyya's circumstantial-state analysis: كما modifies an action, not the agent's state; an unspoken emphatic state is unnecessary, and if explicit it must attach to a verbal noun or its pronoun.
rows.anchor: لأن الكاف الداخلة على ما المصدرية هي من صفات الفعل، لا من صفات الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God curses those who conceal revealed rulings after they were clarified; repentance requires reform and disclosure, since concealment corrupts religious guidance and clarification reverses its harm.
rows.anchor: ثم استثنى من تاب وأصلح، وبين ما كتم. ولم يكتف بالتوبة فقط حتى أضاف إليها الإصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepts repentance from any sin, however grave, and describes Himself with the intensive forms التواب الرحيم.
rows.anchor: وأنه تعالى لا يتعاظم عنده ذنب، وإن كان أعظم الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who die in disbelief remain under God's, the angels', and people's curse forever, without lighter punishment or respite.
rows.anchor: وأنهم خالدون في اللعنة، غير مخفف عنهم العذاب، ولا مرجئون إلى وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because much unbelief arises from taking gods beside God, the passage affirms that deity is one, indivisible, without likeness in attributes, and that God alone rewards and punishes.
rows.anchor: أخبر تعالى أن الإله هو واحد لا يتعدد ولا يتجزأ، ولا له مثيل في صفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs begin with the invention of the upper heavens and dense earth, and the alternation of night and day through the motions God placed in the upper cosmos.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بذكر اختراع الأفلاك العلوية، والجرم الكثيف الأرضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships move back and forth for human benefit through what God placed in the lower world; rain, the earth's revival, and animal life join the upper and lower realms.
rows.anchor: واختلاف الفلك ذاهبة وآئبة بما ينفع الناس الناشئ ذلك عما أودع في العالم السفلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Winds and clouds between heaven and earth complete the blessings that sustain marine and terrestrial human interests.
rows.anchor: إذ كان بذلك تتم النعمة المقتضية لصلاح العالم في منافعهم البحرية والبرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These cosmic signs guide rational people to God's oneness and exclusive divinity; idols cannot produce any of them and, like all creatures, depend on God and change.
rows.anchor: إذ من عبدوه من دون الله يعلمون قطعا أنه لا يمكنه اقتدار على شيء مما تضمنته هذه الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some people make rivals whom they love as they love God, equating Creator and created; believers love God more intensely than idolaters love their idols.
rows.anchor: وأنهم يؤثرونهم ويحبونهم مثل محبة الله، فهم يسوون بين الخالق والمخلوق في المحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the wrongdoers see the punishment that follows taking rivals, the scene would be tremendous; their rivals have no power to avert it because every power belongs to God.
rows.anchor: لأن جميع القوى والقدر هي لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At punishment, leaders disavow followers and their former bonds disappear; followers wish impossibly to return and disown their leaders, but God has decreed there is no return.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى تبرؤ المتبوعين من التابعين وقت رؤية العذاب وزالت المودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After seeing the punishment and severed ties, people see their deeds as regrets too late to help, compounding their pain, then face everlasting punishment.
rows.anchor: أراهم أعمالهم ندامات حيث لا ينفع الندم، ليتضاعف بذلك الألم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الصيام and الصوم are verbal nouns of صام; in Arabic the word applies broadly to anyone or anything abstaining, including Mary's silence, still wind, and animals withholding food or movement.
rows.anchor: والعرب تسمي كل ممسك صائما، ومنه الصوم في الكلام إني نذرت للرحمن صوما

rows.speaker: النابغة الذبياني
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha's image of fasting horses shows that صيام can mean refraining from running amid battle dust.
rows.anchor: وقال النابغة الذبياني: خيل صيام وخيل غير صائمة ... تحت العجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word also describes an unmoving mill-beast and the midday heat standing still or intensifying, as illustrated by Arabic rajaz and other poetry.
rows.anchor: وتسمى الدابة التي لا تدور: الصائمة، قال الراجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مصام النجوم denotes the stars' pause or stillness.
rows.anchor: ومصام النجوم، إمساكها عن اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In legal usage, fasting is abstaining from specified things during a specified time, with the details explained in jurisprudence.
rows.anchor: وأما الحقيقة الشرعية فهو: إمساك عن أشياء مخصوصة في وقت مخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الطاقة and الطوق mean capability and power; أبو ذؤيب's line illustrates the root's sense of carrying within one's capacity.
rows.anchor: الطاقة، والطوق: القدرة والاستطاعة، ويقال: طاق وأطاق كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The month is a time span marked by the moon's first concealment through its disappearance and renewed appearance; it is named for its public visibility and people's need for it.
rows.anchor: وهو: المدة الزمانية التي يكون مبدؤ الهلال فيها خافيا إلى أن يستسر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines الشهر as the new moon; a poetic comparison to a fingernail supports its small, visible appearance.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الشهر الهلال. قال. والشهر مثل قلامة الظفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An old Arabic poem uses ناتق as a pre-Islamic name for Ramadan and depicts its warriors leaving the battlefield.
rows.anchor: وفي ناتق أحلت لدى حرمة الوغى ... وولت على الأدبار فرسان خثعما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects to deriving Ramadan as a verbal noun from burning: this pattern is not a regular verbal noun of an intransitive verb, so treating the name as independently coined is preferable.
rows.anchor: ويحتاج في تحقيق أنه مصدر إلى صحة نقل لأن فعلانا ليس مصدر فعل اللازم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari derives رمضان as a verbal noun from burning in the intense heat; the author objects that this pattern is not a regular verbal noun of an intransitive verb and prefers treating it as an independent name.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الرمضان، مصدر رمض إذا احترق من الرمضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further proposed source is الرمض, a rain before autumn that cleans dust from the earth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو مشتق من الرمض، وهو مطر يأتي قبل الخريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: القرآن is originally a verbal noun of قرأ, later used for the revealed book by naming the object through its source; with hamza it can mean gathering, while the unhamzated form may reflect transfer and deletion or a root meaning joining.
rows.anchor: القرآن: مصدر قرأ قرآنا. قال حسان، رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects deriving Qur'an from gathering water in a basin because that verb belongs to a different root-pattern.
rows.anchor: ومن زعم من: قريت الماء في الحوض، أي: جمعته، فقوله فاسد لاختلاف المادتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: السفر is linked to uncovering: a woman casts off her veil, a traveler removes his turban, and dawn or a face becomes bright; a traveler is exposed to open land and a written book reveals its contents.
rows.anchor: الأزهري سمي مسافرا لكشف قناع الكن عن وجهه، وبروزه للأرض الفضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اليسر means ease, while يسر may also mean becoming wealthy and الميسر denotes gambling; the left hand is named optimistically or because it assists the right.
rows.anchor: اليسر: السهولة، يسر: سهل، ويسر: سهل، وأيسر: استغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: العسر means hardship or constriction, and الإكمال means completion.
rows.anchor: العسر: الصعوبة والضيق، ومنه أعسر إعسارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An answer may stand for hearing because response follows hearing; the true response delivers what the supplicant requested, and أجاب and استجاب are synonymous.
rows.anchor: وجهة المجاز بينهما ظاهرة لأن الإجابة مترتبة على السماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of أجاب is related to cutting or selecting: the respondent apportions to the asker what was requested; rain and vegetation likewise answer sky and earth.
rows.anchor: فكأن المجيب اقتطع للسائل ما سأل أن يعطاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الرشد is the opposite of error; the verb has two vocalized forms, and related derivatives refer to guidance, a straight route, lawful descent, and destinations.
rows.anchor: الرشد: ضد الغي، يقال: رشد بالفتح، رشدا، ورشد بالكسر رشدا

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-ʿAjjaj's verse uses رفث for indecent speech.
rows.anchor: قال العجاج: ورب أسراب حجيج كظم ... عن اللغا ورفث التكلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والزجاج
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Zajjaj, and others take رفث as a comprehensive term for what a man desires with a woman; Ibn Abbas's verse and his reply place this usage in sexual relations, including during pilgrimage discussion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، والزجاج، وغيرهما: الرفث كلمة جامعة لكل ما يريده الرجل من المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A separate interpretation restricts رفث to intercourse and cites a poet describing women as avoiding men's sexual advances.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الرفث: الجماع، واستدل على ذلك بقول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting is introduced as the fourth pillar after faith, prayer, and almsgiving.
rows.anchor: فأتى بهذا الركن الرابع، وهو: الصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three obligations use passive كتب with God omitted as understood; this suits burdensome duties, whereas active constructions for mercy and faith suit comfort and glad tidings, a subtle rhetorical choice.
rows.anchor: وحذف الفاعل للعلم به، إذ هو: الله تعالى، لأنها مشاق صعبة على المكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active voice in the command imposed on the Jews suits their rebelliousness and resistance to prophets, so the different grammatical forms fit different audiences.
rows.anchor: ففرق بين الخطابين لافتراق المخاطبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are directly addressed for the distinct fasting duty to make them attend, while the prior obligation followed the same sequence as another and needed no fresh call.
rows.anchor: ونادى المؤمنين عند إعلامهم بهذا المكتوب الثالث الذي هو الصيام لينبههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase identifying those obligated precedes the direct object because the addressees are most salient; they learn first that they are addressed, then await the duty.
rows.anchor: وقدم الجار والمجرور على المفعول به الصريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in الصيام is anaphoric if earlier communities had fasted, and generic if they had not.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام في: الصيام، للعهد إن كانت قد سبقت تعبداتهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الصيام uses the common verbal-noun pattern فعال rather than فعول for a hollow واوي verb because two wāws together are heavy, though a few forms retain the original pattern.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن الفعول وإن كان الأصل لاستثقال الواوين

rows.speaker: الشعبي وآخرون
rows.claim: One account says fasting was prescribed to Christians before Islam; generation by generation they added days until it reached fifty, then moved it to a solar season because summer heat made it difficult.
rows.anchor: قال الشعبي وغيره: والمصوم معين وهو رمضان فرض على الذين من قبلنا وهم النصارى

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash says a report about this account comes from Dagfal, al-Hasan, and al-Suddi.
rows.anchor: قال النقاش: وفي ذلك حديث عن دغفل، والحسن، والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says a king vowed ten added days after recovering from illness, followed by later rulers adding seven and then three.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل مرض ملك من ملوكهم، فنذر إن برىء أن يزيد فيه عشرة أيام

rows.speaker: السدي والربيع وأبو العالية
rows.claim: They say early Muslims fasted, then after sleeping could neither eat, drink, nor have intercourse; this rule was abrogated after the incidents of Umar and Qays ibn Sirma.
rows.anchor: ثم انتبهوا في الليل، وكان ذلك في أول الإسلام، ثم نسخ بسبب عمر، وقيس بن صرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Jews shared this fasting rule, so الذين من قبلنا means Jews and Christians; another view limits the reference to Jews, after whose practice Ramadan fasting replaced the earlier duty.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الذين من قبلنا: هم اليهود خاصة، فرض علينا كما فرض عليهم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says fasting trains a person against bodily desires and, as far as possible, imitates the higher assembly.
rows.anchor: للصوم فائدتان رياضة الإنسان نفسه عن ما تدعوه إليه من الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comparing the fast to an earlier obligation eases it for believers because fasting is difficult.
rows.anchor: وحكمة التشبيه أن الصوم عبادة شاقة، فإذا ذكر أنه كان مفروضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax attaches لعلكم تتقون to the prescription, making hoped-for piety the purpose of the fast; it may mean joining the pious group because fasting marks them.
rows.anchor: الظاهر: تعلق، لعل بكتب، أي: سبب فرضية الصوم هو رجاء حصول التقوى لكم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ataa interprets taqwa here as shielding oneself from Hell by avoiding sins, since fasting weakens desire and restrains it.
rows.anchor: تجعلون بينكم وبين النار وقاية بترك المعاصي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the purpose is avoiding food, drink, and intercourse during the required fasting hours, or more broadly fasting's prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تتقون الأكل والشرب والجماع في وقت وجوب الصوم، قاله السدي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj interprets taqwa as avoiding sins because fasting restrains many desires of the self.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تتقون المعاصي، لأن الصوم يكف عن كثير ما تشوق إليه النفس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet recommends fasting for one unable to marry, describing it as a restraint of sexual desire.
rows.anchor: فعليه بالصوم فإن الصوم له وجاء

rows.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى وجمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: If the prescribed fast is Ramadan, معدودات refers to its days; calling them countable eases the obligation by suggesting a small, finite number.
rows.anchor: معدودات، تسهيلا على المكلف بأن هذه الأيام يحصرها العد ليست بالكثيرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
rows.claim: If the duty was three days monthly, possibly with Ashura, then معدودات refers to those days as the earlier communities' fast.
rows.anchor: فيكون قوله: أياما معدودات عني بها هذه الأيام، وإلى هذا ذهب ابن عباس، وعطاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء وقتادة
rows.claim: They identify the days as the white days, with disagreement whether these are the 12th–14th or the 13th and two following days; a report supports the latter if authentic.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وعطاء، وقتادة: هي الأيام البيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes say three days each month and Ashura were obligatory early in Islam for seventeen months before Ramadan abrogated them; Ibn Abbas calls the qibla and fast the first post-Hijra abrogations, while another report dates Ramadan to shortly before Badr.
rows.anchor: فصاموا كذلك في سبعة عشر شهرا، ثم نسخ بصوم رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says those days began as voluntary fasting, became obligatory, and were then abrogated.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان صوم تلك الأيام تطوعا، ثم فرض، ثم نسخ

rows.speaker: محمد بن أبي الفضل المرسي
rows.claim: Al-Mursi argues the days were not Ramadan: a report says Ramadan abrogated earlier fasts, the sick/traveler ruling would otherwise repeat, and fidya implies a choice unlike obligatory Ramadan fasting.
rows.anchor: بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «صوم رمضان نسخ كل صوم»

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله محمد بن أبي الفضل المرسي
rows.claim: Al-Mursi also treats the repeated ruling for the sick and traveler and the verse's fidya as evidence that this earlier fast was different from Ramadan.
rows.anchor: ولأنه تعالى ذكر المريض والمسافر في هذه الآية ثم ذكر حكمها في الآية الآتية بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority's view that the days are Ramadan is stronger: the next verse explicitly identifies Ramadan, and the unspecified prescription can cover any duration before being clarified.
rows.anchor: وأكثر المحققين على أن المراد بالأيام: شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers the objections by reading the earlier hadith as abrogating prior-scriptural or earlier communal fasts and the repeated sick/traveler rule as clarification after residents' choice was replaced by a binding fast.
rows.anchor: وأما الخبر فيمكن أن يحمل على نسخ كل صوم وجب في الشرائع المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever interpretation is adopted, some abrogation is required; the text's recitation order does not prove its revelation order.
rows.anchor: والاتصال في التلاوة لا يوجب الاتصال في النزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أيّاما is accusative by an implied command, صوموا أياما; attributing it directly to الصيام, as al-Zamakhshari does, incorrectly separates a verbal noun from its complement with unrelated كما كتب.
rows.anchor: وتقديره: صوموا أياما معدودات، وجوزوا أن يكون منصوبا بقوله: الصيام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attaches أياما to the verbal noun الصيام, comparing it with intending to leave on Friday; the author rejects this parsing for intervening material.
rows.anchor: وهو اختيار الزمخشري، إذ لم يذكره غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also rejects treating أياما as a time adverb of كتب or as a second object by extension: the writing itself does not occur within the days, only the commanded fast does.
rows.anchor: وأجازوا أيضا انتصاب: أياما، على الظرف، والعامل فيه كتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting may be voluntary or obligatory; obligatory fasts are time-designated (Ramadan and timed vows) or owed (make-up Ramadan, untimed vows, expiation).
rows.anchor: والصوم: نفل وواجب، والواجب معين الزمان، وهو: صوم رمضان والنذر المعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists agree that fasting requires intention but differ about its timing; Abu Hanifa allows a daytime intention through noon for Ramadan, a timed vow, and voluntary fasts, but requires night intention for make-up and expiation fasts.
rows.anchor: وأجمعوا على اشتراط النية في الصوم، واختلفوا في زمانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel distance permitting a fast-break differs: Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, al-Thawri, and Abu Hanifa say three days; a Bukhari report has the first two breaking and shortening prayer at four post-stations (sixteen farsakhs), while another report from Abu Hanifa gives two days and part of a third, measured at an ordinary pace.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عمر، وابن عباس، والثوري وأبو حنيفة: ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik variously sets the distance at the prayer-shortening journey, a day and night, forty-eight miles, forty-two or forty-six; the school also reports thirty miles, while another view says three.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: مسافة الفطر مسافة القصر، وهي يوم وليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that travel for worship, kinship, or necessary livelihood permits breaking the fast.
rows.anchor: وأجمعوا على أن سفر الطاعة من جهاد وحج وصلة رحم وطلب معاش ضروري مبيح

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says breaking the fast is more clearly allowed on commercial or otherwise permitted travel, while prohibition is the stronger view for sinful travel.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والقول بالإجازة أظهر، وكذلك سفر المعاصي مختلف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A traveler may not decide to spend the night fasting-free before travel begins; jurists also say an intending traveler cannot break fast before leaving home, though they differ on consequences and departure point.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أنه لا يجوز لمؤمل السفر أن يفطر قبل أن يخرج

rows.speaker: أشهب
rows.claim: Ashhab says someone who breaks fast at home then travels owes nothing whether or not the trip occurs; Sahnun requires expiation either way, while Isa from Ibn al-Qasim requires only that day's make-up.
rows.anchor: فإن أفطر فقال أشهب: لا يلزمه شيء سافر، أو لم يسافر

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reportedly intended travel, dressed for it, saddled his mount, ate, and then rode; Hasan allows eating at home on the departure day, Ahmad only after passing houses, and Ishaq only after placing a foot in the saddle.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أنس أنه أفطر وقد أراد السفر، ولبس ثياب السفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a person starts the day healthy then becomes ill, he may break the remainder; if the day starts in town and travel begins later, Ibn Umar, al-Shabi, Ahmad, and Ishaq allow breaking, unlike al-Zuhri, Malik, al-Awzai, Abu Hanifa, Shafi, and others.
rows.anchor: ومن أصبح صحيحا ثم اعتل أفطر بقية يومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most jurists require only make-up for breaking during a day one later travels; Ibn Kinanah and Ibn al-Arabi add expiation, which Ibn Abd al-Barr rejects as an obligation not established by God.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمر بن عبد البر: ليس بشيء، لأن الله أباح له الفطر

rows.speaker: الثوري وأبو حنيفة والأوزاعي والشافعي
rows.claim: The apparent wording permits a traveler to break fast even after beginning the day intending to fast while traveling, without excuse or expiation; Malik requires make-up and expiation in one report, but most of his followers deny expiation.
rows.anchor: وظاهر قوله: أو على سفر إباحة الفطر للمسافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أو على سفر is syntactically accusative as a complement of كان, and أو distinguishes types; saying 'on a journey' portrays chosen control over travel unlike involuntary illness.
rows.anchor: وموضع أو على سفر، نصب لأنه معطوف على خبر: كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read فعدة nominative with an omitted predicate or subject; an accusative reading implies a command to fast a number of replacement days.
rows.anchor: فعدة من أيام أخر قراءة الجمهور برفع عدة على أنه مبتدأ محذوف الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional omits an intermediate sense such as 'if he breaks fast, then a number is due'; several Arabic passages likewise omit a verb needed to complete the sequence.
rows.anchor: وبين الشرط وجوابه محذوف به يصح الكلام، التقدير: فافطر فعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عدة means a counted quantity; it is indefinite for concision because only the days missed are due, with من أيام modifying it and أخر modifying أيام.
rows.anchor: والعدة هي المعدود، فكان التنكير أخصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For non-rational plurals, Arabic permits either feminine-singular or feminine-plural adjectives, explaining معدودة and معدودات; أخر is preferred to أخرى here to avoid ambiguity in attachment.
rows.anchor: وصفة الجمع الذي لا يعقل تارة يعامل معاملة الواحدة المؤنثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although أخرى could describe أيام, it could be mistaken for an adjective to عدة because case endings are unclear; أخر clearly modifies أيام through a distinct inflection.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن أن يوصف الأيام بوصف الواحدة المؤنث، فكان، يكون: من أيام أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two forms of أخرى differ: أخر is an indeclinable plural meaning 'other', whereas أخرى, plural أُخريات, means later/next; the forms differ in grammar and meaning.
rows.anchor: وأما اختلاف المدلول: فلأن مدلول أخرى، التي جمعها أخر التي لا تتصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آخر meaning 'another' must belong to the same kind as its referent; a cited poem calls a man's daughter his neighbor to make that usage possible.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز: اشتريت هذا الفرس وحمارا آخر، لأن الحمار ليس من جنس الفرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists who permit a traveler to fast without make-up assume an omitted phrase in the verse; opponents argue the unelided surface requires make-up even for one who fasts while traveling.
rows.anchor: واتفقت الصحابة ومن بعدهم من التابعين وفقهاء الأمصار على جواز الصوم للمسافر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reportedly says the traveler who fasts must make it up; related fringe views are ascribed by Ibn Atiyya to Umar, Ibn Umar, and Ibn Abbas, while Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf compares such a traveler to a resident who breaks fast.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي هريرة أنه قال: من صام في السفر فعليه القضاء

rows.speaker: ابن حزم
rows.claim: Ibn Hazm says even a mile of sinful travel requires breaking fast outside Ramadan once buildings are left; a sick person may break, then make up, and fasting is disliked but valid.
rows.anchor: ويجب على من سافر ولو عاصيا ميلا فصاعدا الفطر إذا فارق البيوت

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء وسلمة بن المحنق وأبو سعيد وجابر وأنس
rows.claim: An established report says the Prophet fasted while traveling, narrated from Abu al-Darda, Salama ibn al-Muhannak, Abu Saʿid, Jabir, and Anas; Ibn Abbas transmits his permission to Hamza ibn Amr to choose either fasting or breaking.
rows.anchor: بالخبر المستفيض أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صام في السفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority infer an omitted 'then break fast' after the conditional, so the traveler may either fast or break.
rows.anchor: وعلى قول الجمهور: أن ثم محذوفا، وتقديره: فأفطر

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه ومالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and companions, Malik, and one report from Shafi say fasting is preferable; Uthman ibn Abi al-As and Anas share this view, with Anas explaining the concession came when people were hungry.
rows.anchor: فذهب أبو حنيفة، وأصحابه، ومالك، والشافعي في بعض ما روي عنهما: إلى أن الصوم أفضل

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي وأحمد وإسحاق
rows.claim: Al-Awzai, Ahmad, and Ishaq prefer breaking fast, as do Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas and several Successors; Ibn Atiyya reports the maxim that whichever option is easier is better.
rows.anchor: وذهب الأوزاعي وأحمد وإسحاق إلى أن الفطر أفضل

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Ibn Hanbal dislikes fasting on a journey; if a traveler fasts then breaks without excuse, al-Awzai and Abu Hanifa require make-up only, al-Layth adds expiation, and Malik has two reports.
rows.anchor: وكره ابن حنبل الصوم في السفر، ولو صام في السفر ثم أفطر من غير عذر

rows.speaker: جابر بن يزيد والشافعي ومالك
rows.claim: A traveler who broke fast and returned that day, or a menstruating woman who became pure, may continue eating without abstaining, according to Jabir ibn Yazid, Shafi, and Malik in Ibn al-Qasim's report.
rows.anchor: فقال جابر بن يزيد، والشافعي، ومالك فيما رواه ابن القاسم: يأكلان ولا يمسكان

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة والأوزاعي والحسن بن صالح وعبد الله بن الحسن
rows.claim: They require the traveler or newly purified woman to abstain for the rest of the day; Ibn Shibrama additionally says the traveler makes it up, while a menstruant may eat.
rows.anchor: يمسكان بقية يومهما. عن ما يمسك عنه الصائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent rule requires making up exactly the number of missed days; the majority follow that count, while Hasan ibn Salih, Malik in one report, and al-Thawri give month-based alternatives that the author rejects as contrary to the text and established practice.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من قوله: فعدة، أنه يلزمه عدة ما أفطر فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is famously read as pronouncing يطوقونه in the passive, from طوق on the pattern of قطع.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن عباس في المشهور عنه: يطوقونه، مبنيا للمفعول من طوق

rows.speaker: عائشة ومجاهد وطاووس وعمرو بن دينار
rows.claim: They read يطوقونه from اطوق, originally تتطوق, with the ت assimilated into ط and a connecting hamza in past and imperative; the author says it is attested as a reading, not merely gloss.
rows.anchor: وقرأت عائشة، ومجاهد، وطاووس، وعمرو بن دينار: يطوقونه من اطوق

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: A group including Ikrima reads يطيقونه, transmitted also from Mujahid and Ibn Abbas; a passive form with initial yaḍamma was also read but some rejected it as incompatible with the root.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة، منهم عكرمة: يطيقونه، وهي مروية عن مجاهد، وابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the geminated ya in this reading weak; the author rejects the objection because the form is تفعيل from طوق, with vowel and glide assimilation producing تطيق.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: تشديد الياء في هذه اللفظة ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The six readings all return to ability: active forms mean they can do it, passive forms mean they are made able; geminated forms can also imply being burdened, like carrying a collar, and hardship.
rows.anchor: فهذه ست قرآت يرجع معناها إلى الاستطاعة والقدرة

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل وابن عمر وسلمة بن الأكوع والحسن البصري والشعبي وعكرمة وابن شهاب والضحاك
rows.claim: Most exegetes say residents able to fast were initially free to fast or feed a poor person, then that option was abrogated by the command to fast when Ramadan is present.
rows.anchor: كان الصيام على المقيمين القادرين مخيرا فيه، فمن شاء صام ومن شاء أفطر وأطعم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والسدي
rows.claim: One view supplies an omitted referent for يطيقونه: people who were young and able but became incapable through old age.
rows.anchor: قاله سعيد بن المسيب والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas offers a view that those who can fast despite an illness may choose to fast or feed, but that concession was later abrogated except for those incapable.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس. وجوز بعضهم أن تكون: لا، محذوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed omission of لا to mean 'those who cannot fast' is misleading and invalid: such ellipsis is licensed in oaths, whereas the cited poetic examples are oath constructions.
rows.anchor: وتقدير: لا، خطأ لأنه مكان إلباس

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Another interpretation applies the verse to elderly men and women who can fast only with great strain, so they may break the fast and pay fidya; a report from Ali and Ibn Abbas supports the un-abrogated reading يطوقونه.
rows.anchor: وأنها نزلت في الشيخ الفاني والعجوز الهرمة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali's report adds the permanently ill, for whom recovery is not expected, to the elderly recipients of the concession.
rows.anchor: وزيد عن علي: والمريض الذي لا يرجى برؤه

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik applies fidya to someone entering Ramadan still owing the previous Ramadan's fast, which they had once been able to perform but later abandoned.
rows.anchor: والآية عند مالك إنما هي في من يدركه رمضان وعليه صوم رمضان المتقدم

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm applies the phrase to sick people and travelers who can sometimes fast without severe strain: they may fast or break and pay fidya, unlike when they cannot fast and must make up days.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصم: يرجع ذلك إلى المريض والمسافر لأن لهما حالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors the first view: the verse initially divided believers between excused sick/travelers owing make-up and able residents who could fast or pay fidya, a choice later abrogated.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من هذه الأقوال القول الأول، وذلك أن الله تعالى لما ذكر فرض الصيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the elderly interpretation, the verse remains operative; jurists disagree whether it covers only elders or also pregnant and nursing women.
rows.anchor: والقائلون بأن الذين يطيقونه هم الشيوخ والعجز، تكون الآية محكمة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports Malik's view that a frail elder is not obliged to pay fidya, though payment is recommended if affordable; this disproves a claimed consensus.
rows.anchor: لأن ابن عطية نقل عن مالك أنه قال: لا أرى الفدية على الشيخ الضعيف واجبة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Shafi requires a pregnant or nursing woman who fears for her child to pay fidya and make up the fast, by the verse's general wording and analogy with the elderly; the Buwaiti report says no feeding is due.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: على الحامل والمرضع، إذا خافتا على ولديهما، الفدية

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa requires no fidya from pregnant or nursing women: unlike the elderly they must make up days, and requiring both replacements would combine two substitutes; Ibn Umar, Hasan, and Hanafi jurists agree.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يجب عليه القضاء، ويجب عليهما

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali's view is fidya without make-up.
rows.anchor: وقال علي: الفدية بلا قضاء

rows.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas say a pregnant woman may break fast and pay fidya without making it up.
rows.anchor: إلى أن الحامل تفطر وتفدي ولا قضاء عليها

rows.speaker: الحسن وعطاء والضحاك والزهري وربيعة ومالك والليث
rows.claim: They require a pregnant woman to make up missed days without fidya; Mujahid and Ahmad require both make-up and fidya, as does Shafi's reported view.
rows.anchor: إلى أن الحامل إذا أفطرت تقضي، ولا فدية عليها

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: For a nursing woman, Malik's well-known view requires both make-up and fidya; his report in Mukhtasar Ibn Abd al-Hakam requires no feeding.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك في المشهور تقضي وتفدي

rows.speaker: إبراهيم والقاسم بن محمد ومالك والشافعي
rows.claim: For each day of fidya, Ibrahim, al-Qasim, Malik, and Shafi (as reported by al-Muzani) specify one mudd; al-Thawri gives half a saʿ of wheat or a full saʿ of dates or raisins.
rows.anchor: يطعم عن كل يوم مدا وقال الثوري: نصف صاع من بر

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and a group specify half a saʿ of food per day; reports from Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayra, Aisha, and others give the elderly the same half-saʿ amount.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وجماعة، يطعم عن كل يوم نصف صاع، من بر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's apparent wording requires food without specifying an amount, so restricting it needs separate evidence.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية: أنه يجب مطلق طعام، ويحتاج التقييد إلى دليل

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Shafi says a person insane for all or part of Ramadan owes no make-up, even if recovering before sunset, because legal responsibility depends on reason.
rows.anchor: فقال الشافعي: لا قضاء عليه ولو أفاق قبل أن تغيب الشمس

rows.speaker: مالك وعبيد الله العنبري
rows.claim: Malik and Ubaydullah al-Anbari require make-up fasting but not make-up prayer after insanity.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك وعبيد الله العنبري: يقضي الصوم ولا يقضي الصلاة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة والثوري ومحمد وأبو يوسف وزفر
rows.claim: They say full-month insanity requires no make-up, but if sanity returns at any point in Ramadan the entire month must be made up.
rows.anchor: إذا جن في رمضان كله فلا قضاء عليه، وإن أفاق في شيء منه قضاه كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read فدية طعام مسكين with nunation, nominative طعام, singular مسكين; Hisham has plural مساكين, while Nafi and Ibn Dhakwan use annexation and plural needy persons with fidya singular.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فدية طعام مسكين، بتنوين الفدية، ورفع طعام، وإفراد مسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nunation, طعام is an appositive explaining the fidya; in the annexed reading, the genitive likewise specifies its kind, since fidya is the required amount and food is broader.
rows.anchor: ومن نون كان طعام بدلا من فدية، وكان في ذلك تبيين للفدية ما هي

rows.speaker: المنتخب
rows.claim: Al-Muntakhab treats the annexation as an adjective construction, with fidya characterized as food.
rows.anchor: وفي (المنتخب) أنه يجوز أن تكون هذه الإضافة من باب إضافة الموصوف إلى الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that adjective analysis: طعام is not a suitable adjective, whether treated as a verbal noun or object noun, because neither construction works grammatically here.
rows.anchor: وهذا ليس بجيد، لأن طعاما ليس بصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural مساكين pairs with a plural subject; singular مسكين tracks the distributive sense, one needy person for each person and each missed day.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ مساكين، قابل الجمع بالجمع، ومن أفرد فعلى مراعاة إفراد العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers attaching وأن تصوموا خير لكم to the immediately preceding choice for those able to fast, rather than to the opening obligation; the clause encourages fasting.
rows.anchor: والظاهر الأول، وفيه حض على الصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن كنتم تعلمون may mean possessing knowledge and discernment, with its object omitted for concision, such as knowing the revealed religion or the reward of deeds; knowledge may also stand for reverent fear.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يحذف اختصارا لدلالة الكلام عليه أي: ما شرعته وبينته لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the counted days are not Ramadan, شهر رمضان begins a new nominal sentence whose relative clause identifies and praises the month before prescribing its fast; الذي أنزل may modify الشهر or رمضان.
rows.anchor: فيكون رفع شهر على أنه مبتدأ، وخبره قوله: الذي أنزل فيه القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that parsing, فمن شهد منكم الشهر is the predicate; the author rejects treating its فاء as extra or comparing it with the relative clause after unrestricted الموت, since this شهر is definite and the clause has a verbal antecedent.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي قالوه ليس بشيء، لأن الذي، صفة لعلم، أو لمضاف لعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If فمن شهد is the predicate, repeating the subject's wording instead of a pronoun links it back and magnifies the month, as in Arabic poetry.
rows.anchor: فأقام لفظ المبتدأ مقام الضمير، وحصل به الربط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating الموت in the cited line instead of using a pronoun illustrates rhetorical magnification and emphasis through repetition.
rows.anchor: لا أرى الموت يسبق الموت شيء وذلك لتفخيمه وتعظيمه

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: If the days already mean Ramadan, al-Akhfash parses nominative شهر as the predicate of an omitted subject: 'the prescribed fast is Ramadan'; al-Farra gives a similar estimate.
rows.anchor: أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف تقديره هو: شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i parses شهر رمضان as an appositive to الصيام; the author objects to the distant separation and says it reverses the usual content relation of apposition of inclusion.
rows.anchor: قاله الكسائي، وفيه بعد لوجهين: أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apposition of inclusion is normally a verbal noun related to a month, as in the verse about fighting in the sacred month and an al-Aʿsha poem; the proposed Ramadan apposition would be reversed.
rows.anchor: لأن بدل الاشتمال في الغالب يكون بالمصادر كقوله تعالى: يسئلونك عن الشهر الحرام قتال فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apposition could be rescued by supplying صيام before شهر, making both expressions name the same referent, but that requires deletion plus a long intervening distance and is remote.
rows.anchor: تقديره: صيام شهر رمضان، فحذف المضاف، وأقيم المضاف إليه مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible remote apposition is to أيام معدودات on Abd Allah's nominative reading أيام معدودات, reported by Ibn Khalawayh.
rows.anchor: ويجوز على بعد أن يكون بدلا من أيام معدودات، على قراءة عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the accusative reading شهر, proposed parses include an implied command صوموا, apposition to أياما, an exhortation الزموا, or attachment to وأن تصوموا; the author rejects the last because a complement of أن cannot be separated from it.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب شهر رمضان على قراءة من قرأ ذلك على إضمار فعل تقديره: صوموا شهر رمضان
